about.title: Lathrop Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Lathrop sits at a crossing point of heavy regional traffic, with I-5 and SR-120 funneling commuters and freight through town alongside busy local routes like Harlan Road and E Louise Avenue. San Joaquin County's 2025 numbers show 217 injury collisions and 288 people hurt in Lathrop alone, with Wednesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. showing up often in the reports. If you were injured in one of these crashes, the days right after matter: evidence disappears, memories fade, and insurance adjusters move fast to lock in a version of events that favors them. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free connection service that puts you in touch with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate what happened, explain your options under California law, and help protect your claim from the start. There's no cost to talk it through, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Lathrop Drivers Reach Out Before Talking to Insurers

items.title: California's Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity — like a public roadway near I-5 or SR-120 — was involved. Talking to an attorney early helps make sure you don't lose that deadline without realizing it.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You Fast
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning even if you're partly blamed for the crash, you can still recover a share of damages — but insurers know this and often try to shift blame onto you early. An independent attorney can help push back before a recorded statement locks in language that hurts your claim.

items.title: No Cap Means Every Detail Counts
items.desc: California doesn't cap non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, which is exactly why insurers try to minimize injuries on the front end. Preserving evidence — photos, witness contacts, medical records — while it's fresh can matter more than people expect.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's usually best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions in ways that can be used to reduce or deny your claim later. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my accident happened on I-5 or SR-120, and a government agency is involved?
items.answer: Claims involving state or local government entities — including issues with road design or maintenance — often carry a much shorter filing deadline, sometimes just six months instead of two years. This is common with Lathrop's mix of state highways and local roads. An attorney can help sort out quickly whether this applies to your situation.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for you. There's no cost or obligation just to have a conversation about your Lathrop crash.
